MTPFN between its bounds: A-only (no transfer) and the Bayes oracle¶

Standalone report, 2026-11-04. Issue #20, branch exp/20-mtpfn. No new runs: it reads the snapshots of notebook 13 (MTPFN on the AIR prior) and pilot 3 (notebook 11) and computes the PPD heatmaps live, on CPU, from the checkpoints.

Question. How well does MTPFN predict the scarce task A from A's few points plus the dense related task B, when it is placed between its two natural bounds?

  • Lower bound: A-only. Pilot 3's clean A-only PFN: the same decoder architecture, trained separately, never sees B. This is what you get without any transfer.
  • Upper bound: the oracle (G-ref). The exact Bayes posterior predictive given the true B function g (the dense-B limit), the true noise σ_A and the true prior over the warp T_θ: a 101² grid over θ at J = 2. It knows g exactly, while every model sees 128 noisy B points, so it is a bound, not an attainable target. It only exists at J = 2.
  • For reference: AIR (pilot 3, q-IS with K = 32, Σ = 0.1; the same seeds and tasks).

Setup.

  • Prior. f_A(x) = g(T_θ(x)) with a random MLP g on the global ECDF scale and T_θ a monotone box-preserving flow with J coefficients. B has 128 points, A has n_A ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5, 10} (nested designs) and 32 query points.
  • Tasks. Pilot 3's evaluation tasks: eval_tasks(J, 256, 777, ecdf), J ∈ {2 (smooth warps), 16 (wiggly)}.
  • Models. MTPFN: 1.84M parameters, 100k steps on this prior, seeds 0–2 (sweep mtpfn/pilot_20261103-132611).
  • Data used.
    • NLLs: results/mtpfn/pilot_20261103-235449, -235620, -235751 (air_diag, seeds 0–2, table ctrl).
    • AIR: results/mtpfn/air_examples/air_pilot3_paired.parquet, copied from pilot 3's air_rb/pilot_20261103-184131 / -211850 / -160447 (seeds 0 / 1 / 2).
  • Metric. NLL per query point in nats on AIR's bar scale (400 bins on [−0.25, 1.25]); lower is better. Means over tasks per seed, then mean ± SE over the 3 seeds.

PPD heatmaps. For example tasks, the predictive density p(y | x, data) over x ∈ [0, 1] for A-only, MTPFN and the oracle, with one column per n_A. Each column of pixels (fixed x) is scaled to its maximum, so the plot shows the shape of the predictive at each x, not its absolute height. Overlays: the true f_A, the PPD mean and A's points.

  • Tasks. The evaluation tasks are generated on the GPU and a CPU regeneration differs, so the first 64 tasks per J were exported once from the run host. results/mtpfn/air_examples/eval_tasks_cuda_first64.pt was written by eval_tasks(J, 256, 777, "cuda", g_norm="ecdf").sub(slice(0, 64)) at commit fb78024, moved to the CPU.
  • Checkpoints. Seed 0's checkpoints (untracked, local):
    • MTPFN: runs/mtpfn/pilot_20261103-132611/0;
    • A-only: runs/_ckpt/aonly_114539/0, a copy of pilot 3's air_rb/pilot_20261103-114539/0.
  • Check. The notebook asserts that its live per-task MTPFN and oracle NLLs reproduce the ctrl table.

Limits. The oracle exists only at J = 2. h = id and B is always related (Z0); an unrelated B is a control, outside the training prior. One architecture size (not the paper's 23 × 512).

1. NLL between the bounds¶

def table(J):
    m = S["mean"].loc[J].unstack("n_a")
    se = S["sem"].loc[J].unstack("n_a")
    rows = [k for k in ("aonly_pfn", "b", "air_s0.1", "air_s0.0", "gref") if k in m.index]
    t = pd.DataFrame({LAB[k]: [f"{m.loc[k, n]:.3f} ± {se.loc[k, n]:.3f}" for n in NS] for k in rows}, index=NS).T
    t.columns = [f"n_A = {n}" for n in NS]
    d = pd.DataFrame(index=[f"n_A = {n}" for n in NS])
    d["MTPFN gain over A-only"] = (m.loc["aonly_pfn"] - m.loc["b"]).values
    if "gref" in m.index:
        d["MTPFN gap to oracle"] = (m.loc["b"] - m.loc["gref"]).values
        d["share of A-only→oracle gap closed: MTPFN"] = ((m.loc["aonly_pfn"] - m.loc["b"]) / (m.loc["aonly_pfn"] - m.loc["gref"])).values
        d["… AIR (Σ = 0.1)"] = ((m.loc["aonly_pfn"] - m.loc["air_s0.1"]) / (m.loc["aonly_pfn"] - m.loc["gref"])).values
    p = per_seed.loc[J].unstack("input")
    dd = (p["b"] - p["air_s0.1"]).groupby("n_a")
    d["AIR better than MTPFN (paired)"] = [f"{dd.mean()[n]:+.3f} ± {dd.sem()[n]:.3f}" for n in NS]
    return t, d.T


for J in (2, 16):
    t, d = table(J)
    print(f"J = {J}: NLL per query (nats, mean ± SE over 3 seeds)")
    display(t)
    display(d.map(lambda v: f"{v:.2f}" if isinstance(v, float) else v))

Controls: what MTPFN does with other B inputs¶

B pre-registered: B's inputs pulled into A's frame with the true warp (x_b → T_θ⁻¹(x_b)). If MTPFN's loss were the warp, this would close most of the gap. B removed and unrelated B (another task's B) are outside its training prior, where B is always present and related: they show what happens when the source is missing or useless.

2. PPD heatmaps against n_A¶

The predictive density over (x, y) for A-only, MTPFN and the oracle as A's points accumulate (columns n_A = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10; the A designs are nested, so each column adds points to the previous one). The leftmost panel shows the task: B's 128 noisy points, the true g (B's function) and the true f_A = g ∘ T_θ. Panel titles give the task's NLL on its 32 query points (seed 0). Examples at J = 2 are picked from the first 64 tasks at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile of MTPFN's gap to the oracle at n_A = 3 (seed 0): a good, a typical and a bad case.

from meta_pfn.experimental.air import reference as R
from meta_pfn.experimental.air.decoder import N_BINS, Y_HI, Y_LO, Decoder
from meta_pfn.experimental.air.prior import flow
from meta_pfn.experimental.mtpfn.model import MTPFN
from meta_pfn.experimental.mtpfn.train import air_batch, nll_per_task

torch.manual_seed(0)
TASKS = torch.load(EXD / "eval_tasks_cuda_first64.pt", weights_only=False)  # {J: Tasks}, first 64 of pilot 3's 256
MT_CK = ROOT / "runs/mtpfn/pilot_20261103-132611/0/tracking/artifacts/model.pt"
AO_CK = ROOT / "runs/_ckpt/aonly_114539/0/model.pt"
BORD = torch.linspace(Y_LO, Y_HI, N_BINS + 1)
CEN, W = ((BORD[:-1] + BORD[1:]) / 2).numpy(), (Y_HI - Y_LO) / N_BINS
mt = MTPFN(1, BORD, d_model=128, heads=4, n_pairs=4, d_ff=512, head="bar")
mt.load_state_dict(torch.load(MT_CK, map_location="cpu"))
ao = Decoder(D=128, layers=6)
ao.load_state_dict(torch.load(AO_CK, map_location="cpu"))
mt.eval(), ao.eval()
G101 = R.grid(101)
XS = torch.linspace(0, 1, 200)

# check: the exported tasks are pilot 3's (live per-task NLL == the ctrl table, seed 0, n_A = 3, first 64 tasks)
t3 = TASKS[2].head(3)
with torch.no_grad():
    live_b = nll_per_task(mt, air_batch(t3)).numpy()
live_g = -torch.stack([R.grid_ref(t3, i, G101)["lp"] for i in range(t3.xa.shape[0])]).mean(1).numpy()
ref = ctrl[(ctrl.seed == 0) & (ctrl.J == 2) & (ctrl.n_a == 3) & (ctrl.task < 64)].pivot(index="task", columns="input", values="nll")
print("max |live − table|: MTPFN", np.abs(live_b - ref.b.values).max().round(5), "| oracle", np.abs(live_g - ref.gref.values).max().round(5))

In [7]:
@torch.no_grad()
def ppd_mtpfn(t):
    tg = dataclasses.replace(t, xq=XS[None], yq=torch.zeros(1, len(XS)), fq=torch.zeros(1, len(XS)))
    x, y, m, xq, _, nf = air_batch(tg)
    return mt(x, y, m, xq, nf).softmax(-1)[0].numpy()  # [200, bins]


@torch.no_grad()
def ppd_aonly(t, n_perm=8):  # average over random A orders (the decoder's rank input)
    return np.mean([ao(t.xb, t.yb, t.xa, t.ya, XS[None], use_b=False)[0].softmax(-1)[0].numpy() for _ in range(n_perm)], 0)


@torch.no_grad()
def ppd_oracle(t, mass=1 - 1e-6, kmax=4000):
    """Grid posterior over θ (J = 2), predictive N(g(T_θ(x)), σ_A²) integrated over the bar buckets."""
    lpost = R.grid_ref(t, 0, G101)["logpost"]
    w, idx = lpost.exp().sort(descending=True)
    k = min(int((w.cumsum(0) < mass).sum()) + 1, kmax)
    w, th = w[:k] / w[:k].sum(), G101[idx[:k]]
    mu = t.g.at(torch.zeros(k, dtype=torch.long))(flow(XS.expand(k, -1), th, t.s_t))  # [k, 200]
    s = t.sig_a[0]
    cdf = lambda b: 0.5 * (1 + torch.erf((b - mu[..., None]) / (s * 2**0.5)))  # noqa: E731
    p = torch.zeros(len(XS), N_BINS)
    for c in range(0, k, 256):
        sl = slice(c, c + 256)
        pm = cdf(BORD[1:])[sl] - cdf(BORD[:-1])[sl]
        p += (w[sl, None, None] * pm).sum(0)
    return p.numpy()


CMAP = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("seq", ["#fcfcfb", "#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#2a78d6", "#184f95", "#0d366b"])


def heat(ax, p, t, title):
    ax.imshow((p / p.max(1, keepdims=True)).T, origin="lower", aspect="auto", extent=[0, 1, Y_LO, Y_HI], cmap=CMAP,
              vmin=0, vmax=1, interpolation="nearest")  # fmt: skip
    fa = t.ga(flow(XS[None], t.theta, t.s_t))[0]
    ax.plot(XS, fa, color=INK, lw=1.3, label="true f_A")
    ax.plot(XS, p @ CEN, color=C[1], lw=1.3, ls="--", label="PPD mean")
    ax.scatter(t.xa[0], t.ya[0], s=34, color=C[3], edgecolor=INK, lw=0.8, zorder=3, label="A points")
    ax.set(xlim=(0, 1), ylim=(-0.1, 1.1))
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=8.5)
    ax.grid(False)


def task_panel(ax, t):
    ax.scatter(t.xb[0], t.yb[0], s=7, color=C[0], alpha=0.6, label="B points (128)")
    ax.plot(XS, t.g(XS[None])[0], color=C[0], lw=1.3, label="true g (B)")
    ax.plot(XS, t.ga(flow(XS[None], t.theta, t.s_t))[0], color=INK, lw=1.3, label="true f_A = g∘T")
    ax.plot(XS, flow(XS[None], t.theta, t.s_t)[0], color=MUTED, lw=1, ls=":", label="warp T(x)")
    ax.set(xlim=(0, 1), ylim=(-0.1, 1.1), xlabel="x")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="best")


def show_task(J, i, title_extra="", note=""):
    base = TASKS[J].sub(slice(i, i + 1))
    rows = [("A-only", ppd_aonly, "aonly_pfn"), ("MTPFN", ppd_mtpfn, "b")] + ([("oracle", ppd_oracle, "gref")] if J == 2 else [])
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(len(rows), len(NS) + 1, figsize=(17, 2.75 * len(rows)), sharex=True, dpi=78)
    task_panel(axs[0, 0], base)
    axs[0, 0].set_title(f"J = {J}, task {i}: the task{title_extra}", loc="left", fontsize=8.5)
    sa = float(base.sig_a[0])
    for r in range(1, len(rows)):
        axs[r, 0].axis("off")
    axs[1, 0].text(0, 0.5, f"σ_A = {sa:.3f}\nmean |T(x) − x| = {float((flow(XS[None], base.theta, base.s_t) - XS).abs().mean()):.3f}",
                   transform=axs[1, 0].transAxes, fontsize=9, color=MUTED)  # fmt: skip
    if note:
        axs[1, 0].text(0, 0.3, note, transform=axs[1, 0].transAxes, fontsize=9, color=MUTED)
    for c, n in enumerate(NS, start=1):
        t = base.head(n)
        for r, (name, fn, key) in enumerate(rows):
            v = ctrl[(ctrl.seed == 0) & (ctrl.J == J) & (ctrl.n_a == n) & (ctrl.task == i) & (ctrl.input == key)].nll
            heat(axs[r, c], fn(t), t, f"{name}, n_A = {n}   NLL {float(v.iloc[0]):.2f}")
            if c == 1:
                axs[r, c].set_ylabel("y")
    axs[0, 1].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower left")
    for c in range(1, len(NS) + 1):
        axs[-1, c].set_xlabel("x")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

J = 16 (wiggly warps; no oracle)¶

r16 = ctrl[(ctrl.seed == 0) & (ctrl.J == 16) & (ctrl.n_a == 3) & (ctrl.task < 64)].pivot(index="task", columns="input", values="nll")
gg = r16.aonly_pfn - r16.b
for q in (0.25, 0.75):

    show_task(16, i, note=f"MTPFN gain over A-only\nat n_A = 3: {gg[i]:+.2f} nats")

Reading¶

Between the bounds (J = 2). MTPFN is much better than A-only (+1.05 nats at n_A = 1 down to +0.21 at n_A = 10) and is 0.20–0.28 nats above the oracle at every n_A. As a share of the possible gain it closes 84 % of the A-only → oracle gap at n_A = 1, falling to 46 % at n_A = 10. The more A data there is, the smaller the share of the remaining gain it gets. AIR closes 90 % → 61 % on the same tasks and is better by 0.07–0.09 nats in every cell. At J = 16 (no oracle), MTPFN gains +1.00 → +0.15 over A-only and is 0.03 nats behind AIR at Σ = 0.1 (level with AIR at Σ = 0).

Per task. The median task is 0.15–0.22 nats above the oracle; only 28–38 % of tasks are within 0.1. MTPFN is worse than A-only on 4 % of tasks at n_A = 1, rising to 11 % at n_A = 10: as A's own data becomes informative, B sometimes misleads it.

What the heatmaps show.

  • The good case (task 53): MTPFN's predictive is close to the oracle's at every n_A, including the bimodal "where is the step" uncertainty at n_A ≤ 2. Here MTPFN effectively infers the warp.
  • The typical case (task 3): MTPFN is a smooth, slightly wide band around B's shape and tightens little with n_A. The oracle commits to the exact local structure much earlier (a sharp plateau and a kink).
  • The bad case (task 2, a strong warp, mean |T(x) − x| = 0.40): the oracle stays multimodal where A has no points (two candidate positions for the rise). MTPFN commits to a single, shifted ramp and gets worse from n_A = 1 to 3. It locks onto one reading of B rather than representing the posterior over warps.
  • J = 16: with one A point MTPFN copies B's shape confidently in the wrong place (task 13: NLL −0.18 vs A-only −0.85). It corrects once A covers the domain.

Controls. Registering B with the true warp helps only at small n_A (+0.12 → 0.00 at J = 2), so the warp itself is not what costs MTPFN the 0.20–0.28 nats. Removing B or giving it an unrelated B is catastrophic: NLL +1.55 / +3.34 at n_A = 1 (A-only: −0.87), and still worse than A-only at n_A = 10 (−1.48 / −0.35 vs −2.18). Both inputs are outside its training prior, but it means MTPFN as trained here has no safe fallback when the source is unrelated.

Summary. MTPFN is a strong baseline. It realises most of the transfer at n_A = 1 but a shrinking share as n_A grows. Its losses come from committing to one reading of B (too narrow where the oracle is multimodal, too wide where the oracle is sharp), not from the warp. AIR, which represents the warp posterior explicitly, keeps a consistent 0.07–0.09 nat edge at J = 2.
